title: Acne vulgaris
subject: rheumatology-dermatology
summary: Offer a 12-week course of a fixed topical combination (retinoid or clindamycin with benzoyl peroxide); add oral doxycycline or lymecycline for moderate to severe acne, never as monotherapy and rarely beyond 6 months; use isotretinoin for severe, scarring or refractory acne with strict pregnancy prevention and mood monitoring.

sections.title: Recognise and assess
items: Open and closed comedones with inflammatory papules, pustules, nodules or cysts on the face, chest and back. Grade as mild to moderate (comedones, few papules or pustules) or moderate to severe (many inflammatory lesions, nodules, cysts, scarring).
Acne fulminans (sudden severe ulcerating acne with fever, arthralgia and raised inflammatory markers): same-day referral to on-call dermatology (NICE).

Look for hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, irregular periods: polycystic ovary syndrome, now termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome by NICE), drug causes (anabolic steroids, systemic corticosteroids, lithium) and mimics (rosacea, perioral dermatitis, folliculitis).
Acne in children aged 1 to 7 years is unusual: look for hyperandrogenism, precocious puberty or an androgen-secreting tumour and refer.
Ask about psychological distress, low mood, self-harm and body dysmorphic concerns, which can occur with acne of any severity.

sections.title: First-line treatment (12-week course)
items: Skin care: non-alkaline (syndet) cleanser twice daily; non-comedogenic, non-oil-based moisturisers, sunscreen and make-up; avoid picking. No specific diet is proven to help.
Any severity: fixed combination of topical adapalene with benzoyl peroxide, or tretinoin with clindamycin, once daily in the evening. Mild to moderate: benzoyl peroxide with clindamycin once daily.

Moderate to severe: adapalene with benzoyl peroxide (or topical azelaic acid) plus oral doxycycline or lymecycline once daily. AAD 2024: doxycycline strongly recommended; minocycline and sarecycline conditional; doxycycline preferred over azithromycin.
Never use topical or oral antibiotic monotherapy, or a topical plus an oral antibiotic together; always combine antibiotics with benzoyl peroxide or a retinoid.
Start retinoids and benzoyl peroxide on alternate days or as short contact (washed off after 1 hour) to limit irritation. Benefit takes 6 to 8 weeks; do not switch early.
Benzoyl peroxide alone if retinoids and antibiotics are unsuitable. If tetracyclines cannot be used, trimethoprim or an oral macrolide may replace them (NICE).

sections.title: Review, hormonal therapy and isotretinoin
items: Review at 12 weeks. If an oral antibiotic has cleared the acne, stop it and continue the topical; if improved but not clear, continue it for up to 12 more weeks. Continue antibiotics beyond 6 months only exceptionally, reviewing every 3 months.

No response: mild to moderate, switch to another first-line option; moderate to severe despite an oral antibiotic, refer. Also refer after 2 failed courses, for scarring, persistent pigmentation, nodulo-cystic acne, acne conglobata or major psychological distress.
Hormonal options for females (conditional, AAD): combined oral contraceptive, and spironolactone; routine potassium checks are not needed in healthy young people on spironolactone.

Isotretinoin for severe acne resistant to adequate antibiotic plus topical therapy, nodulo-cystic acne, acne conglobata or acne causing scarring: 0.5 to 1 mg/kg/day (lower if adverse effects) to a cumulative 120 to 150 mg/kg, or stop earlier if clear with no new lesions for 4 to 8 weeks.

On isotretinoin: daily dosing preferred (AAD); check liver enzymes and lipids (routine CBC not needed); counsel and monitor for low mood, suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction, and stop with urgent review if severe.
Maintenance for frequent relapse: adapalene with benzoyl peroxide (or adapalene, azelaic acid or benzoyl peroxide alone), reviewed after 12 weeks.

sections.title: Pregnancy prevention, pregnancy and age limits
items: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic: follow the national pregnancy prevention programme (for example MHRA PPP, US iPLEDGE): highly effective contraception from at least 1 month before, throughout and for 1 month after treatment, with pregnancy tests before, during (usually monthly) and after stopping.
Topical retinoids and oral tetracyclines are contraindicated in pregnancy and when planning pregnancy. Tetracyclines are not used under 12 years (NICE) or under 8 years (AAD).
In pregnancy: benzoyl peroxide with clindamycin (with caution) or azelaic acid topically; oral erythromycin if an oral antibiotic is essential.
People with acne wanting hormonal contraception: prefer a combined oral contraceptive over the progestogen-only pill.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Antibiotic monotherapy, or long courses without benzoyl peroxide, driving resistance.
Switching treatment before 8 to 12 weeks of adherent use.
Delaying referral for scarring or nodulo-cystic acne: scars are permanent.
Missing depression or suicidal thoughts before and during isotretinoin.
Topical steroid or steroid combination creams on the face, which cause steroid acne and rosacea-like eruptions.

drugs.name: Adapalene 0.1% with benzoyl peroxide 2.5% gel
drugs.dose: Apply thinly once daily in the evening to affected areas
drugs.notes: Any severity and maintenance. Not in pregnancy. Irritation, photosensitivity, bleaches fabric.

drugs.name: Clindamycin 1% with benzoyl peroxide gel
drugs.dose: Apply once daily in the evening
drugs.notes: Mild to moderate acne; can be used with caution in pregnancy.

drugs.name: Tretinoin 0.025% with clindamycin 1% gel
drugs.dose: Apply once daily in the evening
drugs.notes: Any severity. Not in pregnancy or breastfeeding.

drugs.name: Azelaic acid 20% cream
drugs.notes: With an oral antibiotic for moderate to severe acne, or alone for maintenance; helps post-inflammatory pigmentation.

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.dose: 100 mg orally once daily with food and a full glass of water, taken upright
drugs.notes: Always with topical therapy; review at 12 weeks; usually no more than 6 months. Photosensitivity. Not in pregnancy or young children.

drugs.name: Isotretinoin
drugs.dose: 0.5 to 1 mg/kg/day orally with food, to a cumulative 120 to 150 mg/kg
drugs.notes: Specialist initiation. Pregnancy prevention programme, liver enzymes and lipids, mood and sexual function monitoring.

drugs.name: Spironolactone
drugs.notes: Females with hormonal acne (off-label); avoid in pregnancy; potassium checks only if risk factors (older age, CKD, interacting drugs).
